lobby.charter: Implement `POST /api/login` (`{email,password}` → 200; bad credentials → 401), `GET /api/me` (→ 200 `{id,email}`; unauthenticated → 401), `POST /api/events/:eventId/registrations` (→ 201 `{id,eventId,userId}`; same user again → 409; unauthenticated → 401; unknown event → 404). Use **exactly one** session transport: an httpOnly cookie, **or** a bearer token returned by login as `{token}` and sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Other server routes get the current user through a helper exported from `src/auth/index.js`; its name and signature are up to the team. After Log in, Register must register the logged-in user and the status element must show "Registered" (or "Already registered" on 409). Your code must work together with the other two agents' code. The shared interfaces are `auth.session` (client transport + `/api/me`), `auth.server` (the helper), and `events.registration` (request/response/errors the UI relies on). Only edit files in your area. Don't add dependencies. Don't commit; your work is collected automatically. Call `dibs_plan` once before editing code, with concrete details for each key you produce or require.

proposal.contractText:
## auth.session contract

### POST /api/login
- Method & path: POST /api/login
- Request: Content-Type: application/json body { "email": string, "password": string }
- Success (200): Content-Type: application/json body { "token": string } — token is an opaque random hex string
- Bad/missing credentials (401): Content-Type: application/json body { "error": string }
- No cookie is set; no Set-Cookie header is used.

### Client transport
- After a successful login the client stores the token in memory or localStorage.
- Every subsequent authenticated request includes the HTTP header: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- fetch calls must NOT use credentials: 'include'; no cookie transport.

### GET /api/me
- Method & path: GET /api/me
- Authentication: Authorization: Bearer <token> header
- Success (200): Content-Type: application/json body { "id": string|number, "email": string }
- Missing or invalid token (401): Content-Type: application/json body { "error": string }
proposal.rationale: Claude (item 43) produces a bearer-token transport (POST /api/login → {token}, Authorization: Bearer header), while Codex (items 46, 48) tentatively defaults to an httpOnly cookie with fetch credentials:'same-origin' but explicitly commits to adopting whichever transport the auth owner chooses. The charter mandates exactly one transport and designates claude as the auth owner (item 43 is the producer). Therefore the bearer-token approach wins. Codex must drop the cookie assumption and switch to storing the token and sending Authorization: Bearer <token>. The contract below pins every detail both sides must build against.

proposal.contractText:
## events.registration contract

### POST /api/events/:eventId/registrations
- Method & path: POST /api/events/:eventId/registrations
- Authentication: Authorization: Bearer <token> header (per auth.session contract)
- Request body: empty / no body required (userId is derived server-side from the token)
- Order of checks on the server:
  1. Validate token → if missing/invalid respond 401 { "error": "Unauthorized" }
  2. Validate eventId exists → if unknown respond 404 { "error": "Event not found" }
  3. Check for duplicate registration by the same user → if duplicate respond 409 { "error": "Already registered" }
  4. Create registration → respond 201 { "id": string|number, "eventId": string|number, "userId": string|number }

### UI behaviour (codex)
- Register button carries data-event-id attribute; on click POST to the above endpoint with Authorization: Bearer <token>
- 201 response → set status element text to exactly "Registered"
- 409 response → set status element text to exactly "Already registered"
- 401 response → set status element to a readable message (e.g. "Please log in")
- 404 response → set status element to a readable message (e.g. "Event not found")
- Any other error → set status element to a readable error message
proposal.rationale: Claude (item 45) requires the events route to call getCurrentUser(req) / requireUser (from auth.server), enforce 401 before 404, and return 201 {id,eventId,userId} or 409 on duplicate. Codex (item 47) produces the UI side: it POSTs to the endpoint with the Authorization: Bearer header (per auth.session contract), shows 'Registered' on 201, 'Already registered' on 409, and a readable status on 401/404. Codex (item 49) requires the server to implement all four status codes. The dependency is: the server (claude) must implement the endpoint; the UI (codex) consumes it. All details are pinned below.

Contract text is right. One correction to the rationale: the endpoint lives in src/events/** (droid's area), not mine. droid should use getCurrentUser(req) or requireUser from src/auth/index.js.

contract.text:
## auth.session contract

### POST /api/login
- Method & path: POST /api/login
- Request: Content-Type: application/json body { "email": string, "password": string }
- Success (200): Content-Type: application/json body { "token": string } — token is an opaque random hex string
- Bad/missing credentials (401): Content-Type: application/json body { "error": string }
- No cookie is set; no Set-Cookie header is used.

### Client transport
- After a successful login the client stores the token in memory or localStorage.
- Every subsequent authenticated request includes the HTTP header: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- fetch calls must NOT use credentials: 'include'; no cookie transport.

### GET /api/me
- Method & path: GET /api/me
- Authentication: Authorization: Bearer <token> header
- Success (200): Content-Type: application/json body { "id": string|number, "email": string }
- Missing or invalid token (401): Content-Type: application/json body { "error": string }

## events.registration contract

### POST /api/events/:eventId/registrations
- Method & path: POST /api/events/:eventId/registrations
- Authentication: Authorization: Bearer <token> header (per auth.session contract)
- Request body: empty / no body required (userId is derived server-side from the token)
- Order of checks on the server:
  1. Validate token → if missing/invalid respond 401 { "error": "Unauthorized" }
  2. Validate eventId exists → if unknown respond 404 { "error": "Event not found" }
  3. Check for duplicate registration by the same user → if duplicate respond 409 { "error": "Already registered" }
  4. Create registration → respond 201 { "id": string|number, "eventId": string|number, "userId": string|number }

### UI behaviour (codex)
- Register button carries data-event-id attribute; on click POST to the above endpoint with Authorization: Bearer <token>
- 201 response → set status element text to exactly "Registered"
- 409 response → set status element text to exactly "Already registered"
- 401 response → set status element to a readable message (e.g. "Please log in")
- 404 response → set status element to a readable message (e.g. "Event not found")
- Any other error → set status element to a readable error message

## auth.server contract

### File
- Path: src/auth/index.js

### Exports

#### getCurrentUser(req)
- Signature: `getCurrentUser(req: Request): { id: string|number, email: string } | null`
- Behaviour: synchronous; reads the `Authorization` header from `req`; if the header is present and matches `Bearer <token>` where `<token>` is a valid session token, returns the associated user object `{ id, email }`; otherwise returns `null`.
- Usage: `import { getCurrentUser } from '../auth/index.js';`

#### requireUser (middleware)
- Signature: `requireUser(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void`
- Behaviour: calls `getCurrentUser(req)`; if non-null sets `req.user = { id, email }` and calls `next()`; if null responds with HTTP 401 `{ "error": "Unauthorized" }`.
- Usage: `import { requireUser } from '../auth/index.js';`

### Notes
- No other session-parsing logic should live outside this file; all server routes must obtain the current user exclusively through these exports.

#### getCurrentUser(req)
- Signature: `getCurrentUser(req: Request): { id: string|number, email: string } | null`
- Behaviour: synchronous; reads the `Authorization` header from `req`; if the header is present and matches `Bearer <token>` where `<token>` is a valid session token, returns the associated user object `{ id, email }`; otherwise returns `null`.
- Usage: `import { getCurrentUser } from '../auth/index.js';`

#### requireUser (middleware)
- Signature: `requireUser(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void`
- Behaviour: calls `getCurrentUser(req)`; if non-null sets `req.user = { id, email }` and calls `next()`; if null responds with HTTP 401 `{ "error": "Unauthorized" }`.
- Usage: `import { requireUser } from '../auth/index.js';`
